goal: Prioritize modern spoken Iranian Persian that gives learners the most real-world comprehension and speaking power.

signalDefinitions.conversationalFrequency: How often the item occurs in contemporary informal Iranian Persian conversation. Prefer conversational corpora and native-speaker evidence over general written corpora.
signalDefinitions.speakerDispersion: How broadly the item is used across different speakers, situations, and conversations rather than being frequent in a narrow topic or by a few speakers.
signalDefinitions.practicalUsefulness: How likely a learner is to need the item in ordinary life: family, friends, food, shopping, transport, work, school, health, phone use, social interaction, and common errands.
signalDefinitions.generativeValue: How much language the item unlocks. Productive verbs, compound verbs, grammar patterns, question forms, connectors, and reusable chunks score highly.
signalDefinitions.modernRelevance: How useful the item is in contemporary Iranian life, including current technology, messaging, payments, transport, and present-day social language.
signalDefinitions.writtenFrequency: General written-frequency evidence. Miller rank is supporting evidence only and must never dominate conversational usefulness.

millerRank.notes: Rank 1 maps to about 100; rank 2200 maps to 0. Values above the ceiling map to 0.

final250.purpose: Formal recognition bridge and wider reading/news comprehension. Everyday items may still appear here, but formal/news material belongs here rather than earlier.

stageRanges.purpose: Immediate conversational survival and highest-transfer spoken forms.
Essential everyday conversation, questions, common verbs, people, time, food, and reusable chunks.
High-value compound verbs, home, shopping, restaurants, transport, and social interaction.
Work, school, health, technology, feelings, errands, and broader daily-life comprehension.
Wider conversational comprehension, TV/dialogue language, and lower-frequency but useful vocabulary.
Formal recognition bridge, wider reading/news vocabulary, and useful lower-priority concepts.

editorialRules: Score concepts, not spellings: spoken and formal variants belong to one stable concept when they express the same core meaning.
Teach the form an Iranian is most likely to say or hear in ordinary conversation first; show formal/written forms secondarily.
Prefer complete productive constructions such as جواب دادن, زنگ زدن, and پیدا کردن over isolated components when the construction is the useful learning unit.
Prefer one learner-relevant English sense per card. Split genuinely different meanings into separate concepts instead of dictionary-style gloss piles.
Raw corpus frequency never overrides obvious practical relevance. A lower-frequency everyday word may outrank a high-frequency government, news, literary, or specialist word.
Modern-life vocabulary may be curated in even when older corpora underrepresent it.
A card may be manually promoted or demoted only with an editorial note explaining why; the numeric score remains visible for review.
Native Iranian review is required before a batch becomes production curriculum, especially for spoken naturalness and register.
